## Overview

`04_KEGG_PathwayConvergence.qmd` asks whether genes from two different cell-type-pair analyses land on the same **curated KEGG pathway diagram**. That's one specific, fairly narrow curated resource. This notebook asks the same underlying convergence question a different way: do genes from independent cell-type-pair analyses sit in the same **functional-association network module**, using STRING's combined evidence (curated databases, experiments, co-expression, and text-mining, not just KEGG)?


```{r setup}
#| label: setup
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)

if (!requireNamespace("STRINGdb", quietly = TRUE)) {
  if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
  BiocManager::install("STRINGdb", update = FALSE, ask = FALSE)
}
library(STRINGdb)
```

## Load the curated significant-LR gene list

Same source as `04_KEGG_PathwayConvergence.qmd`: `significant_lr_pairs.csv`, exported by `03c_crossModality_plots.qmd`'s "Export the curated (3-metric-agreement) significant LR pairs" section.

```{r load-lr-lists}
#| label: load-lr-lists

split_complex <- function(x) stringr::str_split(x, "_")

out_dir <- file.path("output", "05_STRING_NetworkAnalysis")
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

sig_pairs <- read.csv(file.path("output", "03c_crossModality_plots", "significant_lr_pairs.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  distinct(spatial_pair, ligand_complex, receptor_complex)

lr_gene_sets <- purrr::pmap(sig_pairs, function(spatial_pair, ligand_complex, receptor_complex) {
  ligands   <- unlist(split_complex(ligand_complex))
  receptors <- unlist(split_complex(receptor_complex))
  tibble(
    spatial_pair = spatial_pair,
    gene = unique(c(ligands, receptors)),
    role = ifelse(unique(c(ligands, receptors)) %in% ligands, "ligand", "receptor")
  )
})

lr_genes_long <- bind_rows(lr_gene_sets) %>% distinct(spatial_pair, gene, role)
unique_genes  <- unique(lr_genes_long$gene)

lr_genes_long
```

## Build the STRING network and map genes to STRING IDs

Mouse NCBI taxonomy ID is `10090`. `score_threshold = 400` is STRING's own "medium confidence" default; raise it (e.g. to `700`, "high confidence") later to check whether clusters hold up on stronger evidence alone.


```{r string-init}
#| label: string-init

string_db <- STRINGdb$new(
  version         = "12.0",
  species         = 10090,
  score_threshold = 400,
  input_directory = ""
)


map_genes_safe <- function(string_db, genes) {
  gene_df <- data.frame(gene = genes, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  rownames(gene_df) <- NULL

  tryCatch(
    string_db$map(gene_df, "gene", removeUnmappedRows = TRUE),
    error = function(e) {
      message("Bulk STRINGdb$map() failed (", conditionMessage(e), ") -- ",
              "falling back to mapping genes one at a time.")
      purrr::map_dfr(genes, function(g) {
        one <- data.frame(gene = g, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
        tryCatch(
          string_db$map(one, "gene", removeUnmappedRows = TRUE, quiet = TRUE),
          error = function(e2) {
            message("  Dropping '", g, "' -- STRINGdb$map() errors on it individually (",
                    conditionMessage(e2), ")")
            NULL
          }
        )
      })
    }
  )
}

mapped <- map_genes_safe(string_db, unique_genes)

unmapped_genes <- setdiff(unique_genes, mapped$gene)
if (length(unmapped_genes) > 0) {
  message("No STRING mapping found for: ", paste(unmapped_genes, collapse = ", "),
          " -- coverage gap in STRING's identifier mapping, not evidence against real biology.")
}

mapped
```

## Cluster the network (k = 4 k-means)


```{r string-clusters}
#| label: string-clusters

n_clusters <- 4

interactions <- string_db$get_interactions(mapped$STRING_id)

score_col <- intersect(c("combined_score", "score"), names(interactions))[1]
if (is.na(score_col)) {
  stop("Couldn't find a combined-score column in string_db$get_interactions() output. ",
       "Columns present: ", paste(names(interactions), collapse = ", "),
       " -- check the STRINGdb version's return format and adjust score_col above.")
}

ids <- mapped$STRING_id

degree_tbl <- tibble(STRING_id = c(interactions$from, interactions$to)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(STRING_id %in% ids) %>%
  dplyr::count(STRING_id, name = "degree")

connected_ids <- intersect(ids, degree_tbl$STRING_id[degree_tbl$degree > 0])
isolated_ids  <- setdiff(ids, connected_ids)

isolated_genes <- mapped %>% dplyr::filter(STRING_id %in% isolated_ids) %>% dplyr::pull(gene)
if (length(isolated_genes) > 0) {
  message("Not clustered (no interaction edges to anything else in this gene set): ",
          paste(isolated_genes, collapse = ", "))
}

score_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = length(connected_ids), ncol = length(connected_ids),
                        dimnames = list(connected_ids, connected_ids))

idx_from <- match(interactions$from, connected_ids)
idx_to   <- match(interactions$to, connected_ids)
valid    <- !is.na(idx_from) & !is.na(idx_to)

score_matrix[cbind(idx_from[valid], idx_to[valid])] <- interactions[[score_col]][valid]
score_matrix[cbind(idx_to[valid], idx_from[valid])] <- interactions[[score_col]][valid]

set.seed(1) 
km <- kmeans(score_matrix, centers = n_clusters, nstart = 50)

cluster_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble(STRING_id = connected_ids, cluster = km$cluster),
  tibble(STRING_id = isolated_ids, cluster = NA_integer_)
)

gene_cluster <- mapped %>%
  dplyr::select(gene, STRING_id) %>%
  inner_join(cluster_df, by = "STRING_id") %>%
  inner_join(lr_genes_long, by = "gene", relationship = "many-to-many")

gene_cluster %>% arrange(cluster, gene)
```

## Convergence: clusters hit by 2+ different cell-type-pair analyses

Same convergence framing as `04_KEGG_PathwayConvergence.qmd`'s `convergence_pathways` table, applied to STRING's data-driven clusters instead of named KEGG pathways.

```{r string-convergence}
#| label: string-convergence

string_convergence <- gene_cluster %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(cluster)) %>%   # drop the "not clustered" (zero-edge) genes
  distinct(spatial_pair, cluster, gene) %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>%
  summarise(
    n_spatial_pairs_hitting_it = n_distinct(spatial_pair),
    n_distinct_genes           = n_distinct(gene),
    genes                      = paste(sort(unique(gene)), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_spatial_pairs_hitting_it), desc(n_distinct_genes))

string_convergence
```

Per-cluster detail, mirroring `04`'s `convergence_detail`:

```{r string-convergence-detail}
#| label: string-convergence-detail

string_convergence_detail <- gene_cluster %>%
  semi_join(string_convergence %>% filter(n_spatial_pairs_hitting_it >= 2), by = "cluster") %>%
  distinct(cluster, spatial_pair, gene, role) %>%
  arrange(cluster, spatial_pair)

string_convergence_detail
```

## Export for downstream synthesis (part 1 of 2)

`gene_cluster` is exported here, right after the k = 4 clustering it's built from; the enrichment half is exported further down once `enrichment_by_cluster` exists. Both feed `06_Synthesis_FunctionBySpatialPair.qmd`.

```{r export-string-clusters}
#| label: export-string-clusters

write.csv(gene_cluster %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(cluster)), file.path(out_dir, "string_gene_cluster.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Full enrichment tables (whole network)


```{r string-enrichment-all}
#| label: string-enrichment-all

enrichment_all <- string_db$get_enrichment(mapped$STRING_id)

fdr_col <- intersect(c("fdr", "false_discovery_rate", "p_value"), names(enrichment_all))[1]
cat_col <- intersect(c("category"), names(enrichment_all))[1]

# Grouped by category (Process/Function/Component/KEGG/RCTM/Keyword/...) then by
# FDR within each, so it reads like the website's sectioned enrichment panel.
if (!is.na(cat_col)) {
  enrichment_all %>% arrange(.data[[cat_col]], .data[[fdr_col]])
} else {
  enrichment_all %>% arrange(.data[[fdr_col]])
}
```

## Export for downstream synthesis (part 2 of 2)

```{r export-string-enrichment}
#| label: export-string-enrichment

write.csv(enrichment_all, file.path(out_dir, "string_whole_network_enrichment.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Network plot, coloured by cluster


```{r string-plot, fig.width=11, fig.height=11}
#| label: string-plot

for (pkg in c("igraph", "tidygraph", "ggraph", "ggrepel")) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) install.packages(pkg)
}
library(ggraph)

cluster_palette <- c("1" = "#2a78d6", "2" = "#eb6834", "3" = "#1baf7a", "4" = "#eda100")

# Drop the "not clustered" (zero-edge) genes from the picture
net_nodes <- cluster_df %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(cluster)) %>%
  left_join(mapped %>% dplyr::select(gene, STRING_id), by = "STRING_id") %>%
  mutate(cluster = factor(cluster))

net_edges <- interactions %>%
  dplyr::filter(from %in% net_nodes$STRING_id, to %in% net_nodes$STRING_id) %>%
  dplyr::select(from, to, weight = all_of(score_col))

net_graph <- tidygraph::tbl_graph(nodes = net_nodes, edges = net_edges,
                                   node_key = "STRING_id", directed = FALSE)

set.seed(1)
ggraph(net_graph, layout = "fr") +
  ggraph::geom_edge_link(ggplot2::aes(alpha = weight), colour = "#c3c2b7", show.legend = FALSE) +
  ggraph::scale_edge_alpha(range = c(0.15, 0.6)) +
  ggraph::geom_node_point(ggplot2::aes(colour = cluster), size = 7) +
  ggraph::geom_node_text(ggplot2::aes(label = gene), repel = TRUE, size = 3, colour = "#0b0b0b") +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = cluster_palette, name = paste0("Cluster (k = ", n_clusters, ")")) +
  ggplot2::theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position   = "right",
    plot.background   = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "#fcfcfb", colour = NA),
    panel.background  = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "#fcfcfb", colour = NA)
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "STRING network, coloured by k-means cluster")
```


```{r string-plot-default}
#| label: string-plot-default
#| eval: false

string_db$plot_network(mapped$STRING_id)
```

## Notes on interpretation

A STRING cluster hit by 2+ different `spatial_pair` analyses is a functional-association-level convergence claim: it means those genes are linked by STRING's combined evidence (some mix of curated databases, experiments, co-expression, and text-mining), not that the original LR pairs interact directly. Same caveat as `04`'s KEGG convergence table.

**Evidence-channel robustness check:** everything above uses `score_threshold = 400` (STRING's "medium confidence," mixing text-mining in with harder evidence). Re-run `STRINGdb$new()` with `score_threshold = 700` ("high confidence") to see which clusters and convergence hits survive on stronger evidence alone -- a cluster that only holds together at the lower threshold is more likely inflated by text-mining co-occurrence rather than real mechanistic support.
